- When sentiment is high (≥0.7) and forecast spikes upward, reduce the peak by 5–10% to avoid overreaction.  
- If sentiment drops sharply (≤0.3) after a recent spike, model should not overshoot downward — cap decline to avoid premature bottoming.  
- Forecast mean should align with recent 7–14 day average of history, not latest 3–5 days.  
- Overshoots after sentiment spikes (especially >0.8) are common — apply a 1–2 day lag correction to prevent premature reversal.  
- If true outcome is consistently below forecast for 3+ consecutive days, reduce forecast by 2–5% per day to reflect mean reversion.  
- When sentiment is low and price is falling, avoid predicting further decline — model should anticipate a rebound within 5–7 days.  
- For 30-day horizon, if forecast is >10% above recent 18-day average, reduce by 10–15% unless sentiment is strongly bullish.  
- If sentiment is volatile (fluctuating >0.35–0.65), forecast should be smoother — dampen volatility with 1–2 standard deviation smoothing.
